song_name: Paapula rakshakudu Yesu goppa dhevaadhi Devudu Yesu

telugu: నాకు తేనె కంటె బహు తీపి యేసు
english: Naaku thene kante bahu theepi Yesu

_note: Split the over-long first block and promoted the pallavi into the empty main slot. Stanza 1 held 6 lines while stanzas 2-7 hold 4 each, so 6 = 2-line pallavi + 4-line verse 1; the split leaves seven uniform 4-line charanams and stanzas 2-7 keep their numbers. Took the first two lines as the pallavi because they are the song title and that reading preserves the source line order. LOW because the record supports a rival split: lines 5-6 ('సర్వంబులో నాకు సర్వమేసు / సర్వశక్తిగల యేసు హల్లెలూయ ఆమెన్') close on 'hallelooya aamen' and read like the sung refrain, which would make lines 1-4 verse 1 instead. Both readings keep every line; only which pair sits in the main slot differs. A source or someone who knows the tune should settle it. No text added, altered or dropped.

english: maanavaaliki idi kaanuka – deva devuni pranaalika

_note: Both 'stanzas' were byte-identical copies of the same two-line English refrain ('Happy Happy Happy Christmas' / 'Merry Merry Merry Christmas'), which is a scrape duplicate rather than two blocks -- the second copy was dropped. The refrain itself is genuinely sung in English, so 'telugu_has_no_telugu' is expected here and no Telugu was invented for it. The real problem remains: this record has a pallavi and a refrain and NO charanams at all, so it needs re-sourcing before it is usable on screen. Held low for that reason.

_edits.before: Happy Happy Happy Christmas / Merry Merry Merry Christmas  (duplicate stanza 2)

_note: One-block song: all 14 lines sat in main_stanza with zero charanams, so the whole song projected as a single unscrollable slab. Split on sense boundaries the lines themselves give: 1-4 are the pallavi (యేసు వైపు చూచుచు ... రెట్టింపు ప్రేమ భక్తితో), 5-8 a 4-line charanam opening on యేసు ఉంటే చాలనే, 9-14 a 6-line charanam opening on యేసురాజు ద్వజము బట్టి and closing the song on యేసుకే జయం అంటు సాగిపోదుము. Telugu and romanised arrays already paired 1:1 and were sliced together; not one character changed. LOW because the record carries no పల్లవి/చరణం headings and no ||...|| chorus-return marks, so the 4/4/6 division is inferred from sense alone -- 4/4/4/2 with the last couplet as a coda is an equally readable reading, and only the published layout can settle it. Two further things flagged but deliberately NOT touched: the romanisation is machine-generated ITRANS-style output ('kRta~mata', 'niSchayambu', 'eDaariloa') rather than the readable romanisation the rest of the library uses, and 'కరుములెత్తి' looks like a scrape typo for 'కరములెత్తి' (raising hands) -- correcting either would mean writing text out of my own head.
